In Tur Rashi is explained thus: such as in the corner of the house there are fixed pegs and two (so in Rashi in the Gemara, preferable to Tur's version that reads "to two") doorways cut in it — one to the north and one to the west; and he fixed the mezuzah inside in the hollow of the northern doorway; and when the door is open it is behind the door — if in the thickness of the pegs there is a handbreadth thickness of separation between doorway and doorway, another mezuzah is needed for the western doorway, since the mezuzah is not in its hollow; and if not — no other mezuzah is needed, for behold it is as placed in its own hollow — end quote. And Mordechai challenged Rashi: from where does he have this? And Ran explained: such as at a doorway of a room that needs a mezuzah, and there are pegs there that are right for this and that; and since there is not a handbreadth between them, one mezuzah suffices — end quote; meaning Mordechai challenged Rashi's explanation: when one enters the western doorway the mezuzah would be to his left, for the pegs would be to the left of one entering there — how does that mezuzah suffice? And therefore one must say that since he fixed it in the northern doorway and there at that doorway the mezuzah is to the right of one entering, it helps also for the western doorway. On this Mordechai challenged "from where does he have this?" — therefore Ran explained there is a room where they enter that room via the western doorway, and for that purpose that doorway was made; and it turns out the mezuzah is to the right of one entering from his house to that room — only via the western doorway; and in this way Maharach Or Zaru'a was strong and extended in his explanation; and in Derishah and Perishah he also extended in explaining this matter of Rashi; and the permission is because since at the essence of its fixing it was to the right, it suffices also for the second doorway that is to the left. And I am astonished at the early and late authorities for an hour: first, why did they not explain Rashi's words literally and all is well — those sages understood there are doorways in west and north as other doorways of a house that leaves in building the wall space of the doorway and reaches to the pegs — how did they understand in Rashi what he wrote "cut in it" — how can the language of cutting be explained here? The clear truth according to my humble opinion: the two doorways are in the pegs themselves cut in it — meaning in the northwest corner stands one thick wide peg, and a large cut is made in it for doorway measure from the north side into the house hollow, and there they enter and exit from north to house and house to north; and another cut for doorway measure from the west side to the house hollow, and there is entry and exit from house to west and west to house; and he made the mezuzah in the hollow of the western doorway — meaning on that side that is right for one entering from west to house, for in that peg itself there is right and left part in the doorway made in it — all is well that he says the mezuzah of the western doorway is plainly as required; only in the northern doorway there is a distinction: if in that peg part separating west from north there is a handbreadth measure, another mezuzah is needed for the northern; but if there is no handbreadth separation, we consider that separation as if it does not exist and the northern too is fit as if also in the western hollow, and one right side for both suffices; and even though for the northern the mezuzah would be far from a handbreadth near the outside — nevertheless it is valid as written siman 289, and all the more here that at least toward the north it was as fitting. And this is also clear in Rashi's language in the Gemara that Beit Yosef brings — only there he mentions southern and western doorway, and it is also in this way, except here the mezuzah must be in the southern doorway in the right part of one entering, and the western doorway is fit with that mezuzah too if there is no handbreadth in the separation, for behold it is right for both. And what Rashi wrote "and when the door is open it is behind the door" — this is not relevant to any reason of exemption or obligation; rather he explains why one doorway is called behind the door in the Gemara; and the Talmud's main intent is to teach us the adjacency of doorways in what way we can understand that the two places are one place — and this is as I wrote; and thereby all is well that the mezuzah was literally to the right of both and in its proper place; unlike what those sages understood that the mezuzah is in the pegs and the doorways are without the pegs — how would the mezuzah join without handbreadth thickness, behold the mezuzah is not at the side of the hollow of the doorway behind it? In what I wrote all is well with Heaven's help; and perhaps from Heaven a place was left for me to explain thus.

baer_heitev.he: שאחורי. פירש רש"י כגון שיש במקצוע הבית פצים קבוע לשני פתחים מחותכים א' לצפון וא' למערב וקבעו המזוזה בפצים בחלל הפתח הצפוני וכשהדלת פתוח הוי אחורי הדלת אם יש בעובי הפצים עובי הבדלת טפח בין פתח לפתח צריך מזוזה אחרת לפתח מערבי הואיל ואין המזוזה בחללה ואם לאו א"צ מזוזה אחרת שהרי היא כמונחת בחללה עצמו ע"כ ויראה מכאן אותן פתחים שהם חלוקים ועמוד באמצע די להם במזוזה א' אפי' אם יש בעובי העמוד טפח דלא מחייב בשתים אלא כשא' בצפון וא' במערב אבל כששני הפתחים ברוח א' אפילו אם יש בעובי הפצים טפח חשוב הכל כפתח א' עכ"ל ומפרש הט"ז דברי רש"י דר"ל דשני הפתחים הם בפצים עצמו מחותכים בו דהיינו שבמקצוע מערבית צפונית עומד פץ א' עב ורחב ונחתך בו חתך גדול כדי שיעור פתח מצד צפון לתוך חלל הבית ושם נכנסין ויוצאין מצפון לבית ומבית לצפון ועוד נחתך שם שיעור פתח מצד מערב לחלל הבית ושם הוי כניסה ויציאה מבית למערב וממערב לבית ועשה המזוזה בחלל הפתח המערבי דהיינו באותו צד שהוא ימין הנכנס ממערב לבית וא"כ המזוזה של פתח המערבי פשיטא שהיא כדין אלא דפתח הצפוני יש חילוק אם יש באותו חלק פצים המבדיל בין מערב לצפון שיעור טפח צריך מזוזה אחרת לצפוני אבל אם אין שם הבדל טפח חשבינן אותו הבדל כמאן דליתי' ומתכשר גם הצפוני כאילו גם הוא בחלל המערבי וימין א' לשניהם סגי ומה שנקט רש"י לשון דרומי ומערבי הוא נמי בדרך זה אלא שבזה צ"ל שהמזוזה בפתח הדרומי בחלק ימין הנכנס ופתח מערבי מתכשר באותה מזוזה ג"כ אם אין טפח בהבדל שהרי היא ימין לשניהם עכ"ל:
baer_heitev.en: Behind — Rashi explained: for example there are in the corner of the house fixed doorposts for two doorways cut in it, one to the north and one to the west; and they fixed the mezuzah in the doorposts in the northern doorway's opening; and when the door is open, the back of the door — if in the thickness of the doorposts there is a separation of a tefach between doorway and doorway, another mezuzah is needed for the western doorway since the mezuzah is not in its opening; and if not, no other mezuzah is needed since it is as though placed in its own opening — end; and it appears from here that those doorways that are divided with a pillar in the middle suffice with one mezuzah even if the pillar's thickness is a tefach — one is not obligated in two except when one is north and one west; but when both doorways are in one direction, even if the doorposts' thickness is a tefach, all is considered one doorway. And Taz explains Rashi's words: meaning both doorways are cut in the doorposts themselves — in the northwest corner stands one thick wide doorpost cut with a large cut for doorway measure from the north side into the house's opening, and there they enter and exit from north to house and house to north; and another doorway measure is cut from the west side to the house's opening, and there is entry and exit from house to west and west to house; and he made the mezuzah in the western doorway's opening — on the side that is right for one entering from west to house; and thereby the mezuzah of the western doorway is plainly as law; but for the northern doorway there is a distinction if in that part of doorposts separating west from north there is a tefach measure, etc.

beer_hagolah.he: ברייתא שם דף ל"ג ע"ב וע"ש בפי' רש"י:
beer_hagolah.en: There is a page in the Qur’an:

mechaber.he: פתח אחד וחלקו בעמוד בינתיים כל שיש היכר ציר בזה ובזה לצד העמוד הרי הם כשני פתחים וצריך מזוזה לכל פתח אבל כל שאין צירים לצד העמוד אין העמוד מחלקו לשנים שאינו אלא לנוי בעלמא:
mechaber.en: One doorway divided by a pillar in the middle—wherever there is recognizable hinge on this side and that side toward the pillar, they are like two doorways and require a mezuzah for each doorway; but wherever there are no hinges toward the pillar, the pillar does not divide it into two, for it is only for decoration.

turei_zahav.he: אין העמוד מחלקו כו'. מבואר בטור דהיינו אם הוא בדרך שאין נבדלין זה מזה אלא אם זה נפתח גם השני נפתח משא"כ אם יש שער אחד גדול וסמוך לו שער קטן כדרך העשירים שאינם רוצים שהשער הגדול יהיה פתוח אלא משתמשים תמיד בקטן רק לפרקים בגדול בזה צריך ב' מזוזות:
turei_zahav.en: The pillar does not divide it, etc. It is explained in the Tur: that is, if they are connected in such a way that they are not separated from each other — if this opens, the other also opens; but where there is one large gate and next to it a small gate in the manner of the wealthy who do not want the large gate to be open, but always use the small one and only occasionally the large one — in that case two mezuzot are required.

baer_heitev.he: מחלקו. מבואר בטור דהיינו אם הוא בדרך שאין נבדלין זה מזה אלא אם זה נפתח גם השני נפתח משא"כ אם יש שער א' גדול וסמוך לו שער קטן כדרך העשירים שאינם רוצים שהשער הגדול יהיה פתוח אלא משתמשים תמיד בקטן רק לפרקים בגדול בזה צריך ב' מזוזות עכ"ל הט"ז:
baer_heitev.en: Dividing it. It is explained in the Tur: that is, if it is in such a way that they are not separated from each other — if this one opens, the other opens as well; but where there is one large gate and next to it a small gate in the manner of the wealthy who do not want the large gate to be open, but always use the small one, opening the large one only occasionally — in that case two mezuzot are required — end quote, Taz.

beer_hagolah.he: תשובת הרשב"א:
beer_hagolah.en: The answer is:

mechaber.he: השוכר בית בחוצה לארץ והדר בפונדק בארץ ישראל פטור ממזוזה שלשים יום והשוכר בית בארץ ישראל חייב במזוזה מיד משום ישוב ארץ ישראל (והוא הדין לשואל בית דינו כשוכר) (ב"י בשם הר"ר מנוח וכ"מ בש"ס):
mechaber.en: One who rents a house outside Eretz Yisrael and dwells in an inn in Eretz Yisrael is exempt from mezuzah for thirty days; and one who rents a house in Eretz Yisrael is obligated in mezuzah immediately because of settling Eretz Yisrael. (And the same law applies to one who borrows a house—like a renter) (Beit Yosef in the name of R' Rabbenu Menachem, and so in the Gemara).

siftei_kohen.en: It is exempt from mezuzah, etc. Because it is not yet considered a dwelling.

beer_hagolah.he: בריי' שם דף מ"ד:
beer_hagolah.en: Barry has a page from D:

beur_hagra.he:
וה"ה כו'. ממש"ש תנ"ה כו':
(ליקוט) וה"ה כו'. כמ"ש בשבת קל"א ב' הואיל ובידו להפקירן ור"ל אפילו לדור בהן ודר בהן פטור דטלית שאולה פטור וכן בית שאולה וא"צ לדחוק שס"ל דכלי קופסא חייבין בציצית דהא לטליתו ופתחו סתמא קאמר דמשמע בכ"ע אסור (עברשב"א בשבת שם ובתוס' דמנחות מ"ד א' סד"ה טלית וצ"ע) והא דאמרינן ר"פ ראשית הגז אלא ביתך ל"ל ה"מ למימר למעוטי דר בבית שאינו שלו וכמ"ש שם בציצית אלא כסותך ל"ל כו' אלא חדא מתרי טעמי נקט (רשב"א בשבת שם ועתוס' דעבודת כוכבים כ"א סד"ה הא. ואע"ג דדרשינן כו'. ובמנחות מ"ד א' בד"ה טלית כו') (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
And likewise, etc. — as written in Tanhuma, etc.;
(Addition) And likewise, etc. — as in Shabbat 131b: since he can renounce them, meaning even to dwell in them and he dwells in them he is exempt, for a borrowed cloak is exempt, and so a borrowed house; and one need not force that he holds vessels in a box are obligated in tzitzit, for regarding his cloak and doorway he spoke unspecifiedly implying in all cases forbidden (see Rashba in Shabbat there and Tosafot Menachot 44a dh "cloak" — requires study); and that which we say in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah "but your house" — why? It is to exclude one who dwells in a house that is not his, as written there regarding tzitzit "but your garment" — why? etc.; rather one of two reasons he cited (Rashba in Shabbat there and Tosafot Avodah Zarah 21a dh "Ha." And even though we expound, etc.; and in Menachot 44a dh "cloak," etc.) (end).

mechaber.he: השוכר בית מאינו יהודי חייב במזוזה:
mechaber.en: One who rents a house from a non-Jew is obligated in mezuzah.

siftei_kohen.he: חייב במזוזה. לאחר ל' יום בח"ל ובא"י מיד וקמ"ל דלא אמרי' כיון שהבית של עובד כוכבים תפטור לגמרי ממזוזה מיהו כל זה היכא דליכא משום סכנה בבית של עובד כוכבים דכה"ג פטור ממזוזה כדלעיל סעיף ח':
siftei_kohen.en: It is obligated in mezuzah. In the Diaspora, after thirty days; in Eretz Yisrael, immediately. This teaches that we do not say that because the house belongs to a non-Jew it is entirely exempt from mezuzah. All this applies only where there is no danger in affixing a mezuzah in the non-Jew's house. Where danger exists, it is exempt, as explained above in seif 8.

baer_heitev.he: חייב. לאחר ל' יום בח"ל ובא"י מיד וקמ"ל דלא אמרינן כיון שהבית של עובדי כוכבים תפטור לגמרי ממזוזה מיהו כל זה היכא דליכא משום סכנה בבית של עובדי כוכבים דאל"ה פטור ממזוזה כדלעיל ס"א עכ"ל הש"ך:
baer_heitev.en: Obligated. After thirty days in the Diaspora, and in the Land of Israel immediately; and it teaches us not to say that since the house belongs to non-Jews it should be entirely exempt from mezuzah. However all this is where there is no danger in the house of non-Jews, for otherwise it is exempt from mezuzah as above seif 1 — end quote, Shach.

beer_hagolah.he: הגהת מיימוני לדעת הרמב"ם וכ"כ סמ"ג בשם הירושלמי בסוף מגילה:
beer_hagolah.en: Gloss of Maimonides per Rambam's view; and so Semag in the name of Yerushalmi at end of Megillah.

beur_hagra.he: השוכר כו'. ירושלמי סוף מגילה וכ"ה בגמ' דב"מ ק"ב א' וע"ל סי' רצ"א ס"ב:
beur_hagra.en: One who rents, etc. — Yerushalmi end of Megillah; and so in the Gemara Bava Metzia 102a; and see above siman 291 seif 2.
